lines.text: An atom is too light for everyday mass units to be convenient. A common reference lets us compare atomic masses directly.

The unified atomic mass unit, u, is defined as one twelfth of the mass of one carbon twelve atom. Thus one carbon twelve atom has a mass of exactly twelve u. The definition selects a particular isotope, carbon twelve, rather than an average carbon atom. Actual atomic masses may be expressed in u, relative masses are ratios to u and have no units.
This fixed carbon twelve reference is the denominator in the definitions of relative isotopic, atomic, molecular and formula mass.
One unified atomic mass unit is one twelfth of the mass of one carbon twelve atom. One carbon twelve atom has mass exactly twelve u. Relative masses are unitless ratios to this reference.
Why does one carbon twelve atom have a mass of exactly twelve u?

One carbon twelve atom has a mass of exactly twelve u. What fraction of that atom's mass is one u? One twelfth One whole Twelve times One sixth ay Divide the mass of one carbon twelve atom into twelve equal parts, each part is one u.
A symbol, isotope label, molecule and ionic formula refer to different entities. Naming the mass correctly tells the examiner which entity you mean.

Relative isotopic mass is the mass of one atom of a specified isotope relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon twelve atom. Relative atomic mass, A r, is the weighted mean mass of an atom of an element relative to that reference, isotope abundances determine the weighting. Relative molecular mass, M r, is the mass of one molecule relative to the reference. Relative formula mass is the mass of one formula unit relative to the reference, used for ionic compounds without discrete molecules. Add the constituent A r values, respecting subscripts, to calculate molecular or formula mass. These are relative ratios without units.
The choice of entity determines the term, an element has A r, a named isotope has relative isotopic mass, a molecule has M r, and an ionic formula unit has relative formula mass.

Relative isotopic mass concerns one atom of one isotope. A r is the abundance weighted mean for atoms of an element. M r concerns one molecule, relative formula mass concerns one formula unit. Each is measured relative to one twelfth of a carbon twelve atom's mass and has no unit.

Consider, in order, chlorine thirty five atoms, chlorine containing a mixture of isotopes, water molecules, sodium chloride formula units. Which sequence names their appropriate relative masses? Isotopic, atomic, molecular, formula Atomic, isotopic, molecular, formula Isotopic, atomic, formula, molecular Molecular, atomic, isotopic, formula ay A named isotope uses relative isotopic mass, an element with mixed isotopes uses weighted relative atomic mass. Water consists of molecules, whereas ionic sodium chloride is represented by formula units.

In one breath.

Chemists compare tiny masses with a fixed reference, one twelfth of a carbon twelve atom. Choose the relative mass term by deciding whether you mean an isotope, an element, a molecule, or a formula unit.
Key ideas.

The unified atomic mass unit, symbol u, is one twelfth of the mass of one carbon twelve atom. Therefore one carbon twelve atom has a mass of exactly twelve u. This particular isotope is the reference for every relative mass in this chapter. Relative masses are ratios, so they have no units, do not attach u to an A r or M r answer. An actual atom or molecule can have a mass expressed in u.

Relative isotopic mass is the mass of one atom of a particular isotope relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon twelve atom. It refers to a specified isotope, such as chlorine thirty five. It is not the mass averaged across the element's naturally occurring isotopes.

Relative atomic mass, A r, is the weighted mean mass of an atom of an element relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon twelve atom. The word weighted matters, isotopes with higher abundance contribute more. For example, a chlorine A r near thirty five point five does not mean an individual chlorine isotope has mass thirty five point five on this scale. Use the A r values supplied by the Periodic Table in your paper.

Relative molecular mass, M r, is the mass of a molecule relative to one twelfth of the mass of one carbon twelve atom. A molecular formula states how many atoms contribute. Relative formula mass is the mass of one formula unit relative to the same reference. This is the term for ionic compounds such as N ay C L or C ay C O three, which form extended lattices instead of discrete molecules.
Method.
Identify the entity named in the question, an isotope, an element, a molecule, or an ionic formula unit.
For a molecule or formula unit, count each atom from the subscripts. A missing subscript means one.
Multiply each element's A r by its atom count and add. Report the result without a unit.
Worked example.

Calculate the relative formula mass of C ay C O three using A r open bracket calcium close bracket equals forty point one, A r open bracket C close bracket equals twelve point zero and A r open bracket O close bracket equals sixteen point zero. There is one calcium atom, one C atom and three O atoms per formula unit. M r equals forty point one plus twelve point zero plus three open bracket sixteen point zero close bracket equals one hundred point one. Call this a relative formula mass because calcium carbonate is ionic. The numerical value is unitless.
Worked example, abundance weighting.

A sample contains only two isotopes with relative isotopic masses thirty four point nine seven and thirty six point nine seven, at abundances of seventy five percent and twenty five percent respectively. Calculate its A r. First check that seventy five plus twenty five equals one hundred percent, all atoms are accounted for. Weight each mass by its share of the atoms, so the more abundant isotope contributes more. A r equals open bracket thirty four point nine seven times seventy five plus thirty six point nine seven times twenty five close bracket over one hundred equals thirty five point four seven. This unitless mean lies between the two isotope masses and nearer thirty four point nine seven, the more abundant isotope. Simply averaging the two masses would incorrectly assume equal abundances. Try with less guidance, Use the same isotope masses with abundances sixty percent and forty percent. The total is one hundred percent, complete the weighted mean yourself.
Check the faded example.
A r equals open bracket thirty four point nine seven times sixty plus thirty six point nine seven times forty close bracket over one hundred equals thirty five point seven seven, with no unit.
Traps.

Trap, Calling thirty five point five the relative isotopic mass of chlorine thirty five. Why it's wrong, thirty five point five is an average for chlorine atoms. Instead, Name the isotope when giving an isotopic mass.
Trap, Calling the relative formula mass of N ay C L its relative molecular mass. Why it's wrong, Ionic solids contain formula units, not separate molecules. Instead, Match the term to the entity.
Trap, Ignoring the two in O two. Why it's wrong, Both atoms contribute to its mass. Instead, Use M r equals two A r open bracket O close bracket.
Exam technique.

For Define, include the exact carbon twelve reference, and include weighted mean for A r. For Calculate, show the atom counts before adding A r values. Check whether the question asks for the mass of a molecule or a formula unit. A relative mass answer needs no unit, even though an actual mass measured in unified atomic mass units would use u.
